name: MS-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Long-serving incumbent Bennie Thompson with large cash advantage
Republican challenger raised only ~$45k with minimal outside spending
Prediction markets price Thompson at ~97% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Thompson: the district leans Democratic by double digits, he is a well-funded incumbent, and Ron Eller's fundraising is negligible with no outside spending to close the gap. Markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold, consistent with a roughly 21-point expected margin.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or a major scandal involving Thompson would be the main way this margin narrows, though a real upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bennie Thompson seeks another term in a Mississippi Delta district that has reliably elected Democrats and carries a double-digit Democratic lean. He enters the general election with about $1.4 million on hand after renomination, while Republican Ron Eller has raised under $50,000 and has no visible outside support. An independent candidate trails far behind in resources.

No public polling or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial edge, and prediction markets, which price Thompson near 97%. The expected margin is roughly 21 points, with modest uncertainty given the absence of direct polling.
